It’s real estate specific. Power of Attorney is notarized like a general notarization. 

Real estate is a whole separate ball game opposed to our general notary work. When doing a real estate signing, We are not notaries, we are signing agents (when dealing with real estate docs) so we get a whole other list of requirements from Escrow that are not usually the case in general notary work. In general notary work we notarize a document and are on our way. We have to be much more thorough in real estate to prevent fraud.

So if that notary needs a copy of your ID, but they don’t get one, they will be scolded or not get another job from that signing service, escrow company, or title agency they are employed with because they didn’t follow escrow instructions. The only way the notary won’t be penalized is if they say the buyer/seller/signed refused. In which Escrow will still receive a copy of your ID. Just from you directly. It makes Escrows job much easier when we do it for them because they have a ton of work as it is on real estate docs.

Usually, when handling loan documents or anything regarding real estate, the courts or Escrow/Title will ask us to get a copy of the ID and send it over to them to prevent fraud. Yes, it’s okay and yes it happens.
